claims.claim_text: Planet operates a wholly-owned subsidiary 'Planet Labs Federal, Inc.' headquartered in Washington, D.C. that serves as the corporate vehicle for U.S. federal/defense and intelligence customers (NRO/NGA/DoD per cohort metadata).
claims.subject: Planet Labs Federal, Inc.
claims.source_quote: We also have a Washington, D.C., office that serves as the corporate headquarters for our subsidiary, Planet Labs Federal, Inc.

claims.claim_text: Planet identifies 'defense and intelligence' as one of three primary verticals (alongside civil government and commercial) and lists it as a strategic growth vertical where it plans to further penetrate via targeted sales and marketing.
claims.subject: Planet defense & intelligence vertical
claims.object_value: defense and intelligence one of three primary verticals
claims.source_quote: We currently serve customers across civil government, commercial and defense and intelligence verticals... We plan to further penetrate vertical markets in which end users are early adopters of geospatial data, such as civil government, agriculture, and defense and intelligence

claims.claim_text: Planet reports $852.4 million of Remaining Performance Obligations (RPO) as of January 31, 2026, with 34% to be recognized within 12 months and 65% within 24 months, framing this as a contracted, multi-year forward pipeline.
claims.subject: Planet remaining performance obligations
claims.source_quote: The Company's remaining performance obligations were $ 852.4 million as of January 31, 2026. The Company expects to recognize approximately 34 % of the remaining performance obligations within the next 12 months, approximately 65 % of the remaining obligations within the next 24 months, and the remainder thereafter.

claims.claim_text: Planet's innovative 'satellite services' model (where Planet builds and operates customer-owned satellites under multi-year fixed-price contracts) represents 'a new approach to how we fund and monetize our next-generation satellite fleets' and is positioned as a forward growth lever.
claims.subject: Planet satellite services arrangements
claims.object_value: multi-year customer-owned satellite contracts (large-scale gov customers)
claims.source_quote: our innovative satellite services model, as demonstrated with recent customer agreements, represents a new approach to how we fund and monetize our next-generation satellite fleets. This model is expected to further align our offerings with market demand and enhance our ability to capture value as we scale our business operations.

claims.claim_text: Planet reports FY2026 (ended Jan 31, 2026) net loss of $246.9 million — a near-doubling versus prior year ($123.2M) and accumulated deficit of $1,449.9M, while simultaneously claiming RPO/satellite-services strength as forward narrative.
claims.subject: Planet FY2026 net loss
claims.object_value: $246.9M FY26 net loss vs $123.2M FY25 (2x); accumulated deficit $1,449.9M
claims.source_quote: we have generated net losses of $246.9 million, $123.2 million and $140.5 million for our fiscal years ended January 31, 2026, 2025 and 2024, respectively. As of January 31, 2026, we had an accumulated deficit of $1,449.9 million.

claims.claim_text: Planet's 10-K names ZERO specific Pentagon Program Elements (PE numbers), zero named DoD programs of record (e.g., no Maven, EOCL, TacSRT, GIDE, JADC2, Replicator, NRO EnhancedView, Tracking Layer named), and zero named DoD prime-contract vehicles. The defense narrative is entirely generic.

claims.object_value: ZERO named PEs / programs-of-record / IDIQs in 120K-char slice
claims.source_quote: (no specific PE, program-of-record name, IDIQ ceiling, or named DoD contract vehicle appears in the 10-K Item 1, MD&A, or RPO disclosure; defense and intelligence references are vertical-level only)
